The best keep still depends on your build.AdvertisementLegacy Piece Trait Tier List: Quick RankingThis is an editorial ranking for the current Gwynn's Shrine game. S and A picks have described effects; B and C are decision bands for rolls whose value depends heavily on your setup.AdvertisementEditorial trait tiers by practical roleTierTrait or groupWhy it is consideredSWorld Breaker; Dominion; Astral CoreStrong repeated damage, control, or defensive value.APhoenix Rebirth; Black Hole; Tyrant KingPowerful survival or control with a more specific use case.BMythical and Legend rolls that match the buildKeep when the live effect supports the main rotation.CTemporary Common and Uncommon rollsUseful while progressing; compare before heavy reroll spending.World Breaker has a clear boss-damage use because repeated hits on one target build pressure. Dominion contributes control and team value in an area. Astral Core combines a defensive shield with a follow-up attack. Those three are broadly useful in different fights, so the order between them changes with the content. Phoenix Rebirth can be a lifesaver in difficult solo clears, Black Hole helps hold enemies together, and Tyrant King favors a durable close-range setup.A rarity label alone is not a fight result. If your current trait keeps a boss run stable, replacing it with a rare name that does not activate in your rotation can be a downgrade. Use the tier below as a shortlist, then compare how often the effect triggers during your actual play.Overall Legacy Piece tier listSee where traits fit with races and clans.What Traits Change in Legacy PieceTraits are a persistent character layer alongside race and clan. A trait may alter damage, protection, control, or recovery without changing your equipped weapon or style.That makes traits easy to undervalue. A strong passive may add an attack after a fixed number of hits, keep you alive through a bad boss phase, or create room for a group to finish a target. The key is trigger frequency. A passive that activates once in a long duel may be excellent for PvP but unimpressive during quick ordinary mob kills. Another that stacks on every hit can be outstanding on a stationary boss yet weak when you constantly switch targets.The current game has a substantial trait pool, and its upper rarities are extremely hard to target through random rerolls. A practical account plan starts with a good-enough effect that supports your current weapon or ability, then saves surplus rerolls for a more deliberate chase. Check current reward details before planning around any reroll source, and do not discard a trait that already solves your hardest content just to pursue a rare label.Current Legacy Piece Traits by RarityThe current Trello-derived roster groups 26 named traits across Secret, Mythical, Legend, Epic, Rare, Uncommon, and Common rarities. The table is a name reference; the tier above ranks combat roles, not every name in a vacuum.Trait names in the current rosterRarityNamesPlanning noteSecretAstral Core, Black Hole, Dominion, Phoenix Rebirth, Tyrant King, World BreakerCompare the signature passive to your main content.MythicalAscension, Flashstep, Limitless, Malevolent, Supreme WillRead the live effect before rerolling a matching one.LegendRebirth, Unstoppable, WarlordEvaluate the exact in-game tooltip.EpicAwakened, Breaker, OverdriveOften useful as an intermediate keep.RarePredator, Sharpened, ViciousJudge synergy with your main damage type.UncommonDriven, Equilibrium, SteadyProgression rolls while building resources.CommonBrutal, Iron Skin, SwiftEarly effects to replace selectively.Secret traits have the most described signature effects. Lower bands include useful temporary rolls, but the benefit of a particular roll depends on its in-game tooltip and the damage source you actually use. Use this list to identify what you have, then read the effect before spending another reroll. A name that sounds aggressive does not necessarily help a defensive build, and a common utility effect can still be useful while you are leveling.How the Leading Secret Traits PlayThe six named Secret traits do not all solve the same problem. Focus on the effect that fills a gap in your build.World Breaker rewards staying on one target across successive hits, making it an obvious boss-farming candidate. Dominion sets up a controlled area and adds team pressure; players who fight in groups or need to hold enemies in place may value it more than a pure personal-damage roll. Astral Core adds a shield and follow-up attack, helping a player survive while keeping pressure on a target.Black Hole is useful for pulling enemies together and disrupting their movement. Phoenix Rebirth turns a lethal moment into another chance, which can protect an expensive attempt or an unfamiliar dungeon run. Tyrant King favors a durable, close-range character that can remain in danger long enough to benefit from its defensive and sustain effects. None of those descriptions means one Secret is automatically best in all modes. Their value changes when a boss is immune to control, when an arena scatters targets, or when a group already provides enough survival.Araya ability guideSee a damage route that can benefit from repeated pressure.Dio style guideCompare a control-focused style route.Best Trait Direction for PvE, PvP, and GrindingFor a single boss, ask whether the trait improves the full damage cycle or protects the run from failure. For PvP, ask whether it creates a safe opening or preserves momentum after a trade.World Breaker is easiest to justify when hits stay on one target. Astral Core and Phoenix Rebirth can matter more in solo PvE where a death resets progress. Dominion and Black Hole have obvious control value in crowded encounters, though a target's resistance and movement still matter. During fast ordinary grinding, effects that need a long buildup may activate too late to influence most packs, while area control and reliable defense can make the route smoother.Compare your trait with the race and clan already equipped. A build with abundant damage but weak survival may gain more from Astral Core than another offensive layer. A tanky race and Berserker clan may free the trait slot for pressure. A cooldown-focused Okkotsu setup can capitalize on a trait that rewards frequent skill use. This is why the site separates traits, races, and clans into detailed pages, even though they all contribute to one build.Race guideMatch a passive stat line to the trait.Clan guideCompare damage and survival layers.When to Keep or Reroll a TraitKeep a trait if it improves a repeatable fight you actually do and you lack enough rerolls to replace it comfortably. Reroll when the effect conflicts with your main damage route or your account can absorb the gamble.Before pressing reroll, write down the trait's job: single-target damage, crowd control, survival, mobility, or a specific support effect. Then choose the job you need next. If the current trait already fills that job, rarity chasing becomes a poor reason to spend. If it activates rarely in your normal content, a different effect may be worth pursuing even if the new rarity is not the absolute highest.When you acquire Trait Rerolls, check the live trait menu and decide a stopping point before rolling. Code rewards change with each update, so read the current reward list instead of budgeting an assumed amount. Armament hardens strikes; Observation supports sensing and dodging. Armament V2 is the later upgrade often called Ryou.AdvertisementHaki progression overviewBranchRouteMain roleArmament / BusoshokuRayleigh; base unlock questsHardens strikes; foundation for V2Observation / KenbunshokuEnel; Hollow and Shinigami questsSense and dodge attacksArmament V2 / RyouMaxed Armament plus Awaken Ryou questsLater Armament progressionConqueror / HaoshokuSeparate Haki branchDominating presenceStart with the branch that addresses your current objective, then read its quest conditions before farming. Basic Armament needs 300,000 Money and the Unlock Armament Haki 1 and 2 quests. Observation needs 1,000,000 Money and its two unlock quests. The V2 route comes after maxing base Armament.Owning the unlock and using it correctly in combat are separate jobs. A quest can ask for Combat style attacks, Haki dodges, or a progression stage. Check the named condition rather than substituting whichever skill deals the most damage.How to Unlock Armament HakiVisit Rayleigh at Ice Land and follow the Armament unlock quests. Prepare 300,000 Money for the unlock.The first task is to defeat 20 Beggars using the Combat style. The second asks for 100 uses of Combat skill Z. Keep the named style equipped and confirm a small amount of progress before grinding the entire counter. A weapon or fruit attack may defeat the target without satisfying a Combat-specific objective.After the Beggar stage, inspect the next quest before continuing to kill enemies. A skill-use counter asks for uses of the named action, which is different from another set of defeats. Watch the progress display so you can see that the game is registering the action you repeat.Avoid an unnecessary stat reset before testing your current setup. Try a short eligible fight first, see whether Combat damage is sufficient, then adjust only what you need. This preserves resources for the later Haki route while helping you diagnose a wrong-style issue separately from low damage.Once the unlock requirements are complete, return to the NPC and check the Haki controls. Try the effect on a familiar encounter before moving into harder progression. The goal is a routine you can use consistently, with enough attention left for enemy attacks and your next quest counter.Armament Haki cardRead the base unlock and named quests.How to Unlock Observation HakiFollow Enel’s Observation route at Hollow Land. Complete 20 Hollow defeats and then five Shinigami defeats, with 1,000,000 Money for the unlock.Keep the two objectives in sequence. A Hollow is the first target; the Shinigami task comes after it. Check the accepted quest and target name before investing time in repeated fights. Reaching a location associated with the route does not mean every nearby enemy counts.After unlocking Observation, practice using it against attacks you can see clearly. Distinguish a successful Haki dodge from manually moving out of range. This becomes especially important when a later quest measures Observation dodges rather than your general ability to avoid damage.For the Star Platinum route, inspect the dodge counter after a short trial. If it advances, continue with the same manageable encounter. If it does not, check the active Stardust stage and Haki state before taking more attacks. An unnecessary high-damage target makes this diagnosis harder.Observation Haki cardRead the unlock branch and its sensing/dodging role.Broken Pedestal quest guideSee where Observation is used in Stardust progression.How Armament Haki V2 WorksArmament V2 / Busoshoku V2 is the later Ryou route. Prepare maxed Armament at Stage 8, 10,000,000 Money, and the Awaken Ryou 1 and 2 quests.Check the base Armament stage before looking for the upgrade dialogue. A base unlock is the beginning of that progression, not proof that the Stage 8 prerequisite is complete. The V2 route is associated with Legacy Island; read the active Ryou task before you leave to farm.One Ryou objective asks for 500 uses of Combat skill Z. Keep the required Combat action separate from a generic skill rotation. If the counter remains unchanged, inspect the equipped style and prerequisite stage before assuming you need a stronger enemy.Treat Armament V2 as its own preparation project. Keep the named base progression, quest completion, and payment ready together. Do not confuse a colour change with an upgrade stage or assume that an Observation task completes the Armament route.When you unlock the upgrade, test it in the same encounter you used for the base setup. Keep other gear and passive choices consistent while learning the new combat routine. This makes it easier to notice how the upgrade fits your attacks without changing several build systems at once.Armament V2 cardRead the Stage 8 and Awaken Ryou prerequisites.What About Conqueror Haki?Conqueror, also called Haoshoku, is a separate branch from Armament, Observation, and Armament V2.Treat its progression separately from the unlock you are currently doing. Completing Rayleigh’s base tasks or Enel’s Observation tasks does not stand in for another named Haki branch. Read the current Conqueror card and the game’s unlock prompt before committing resources to that path.For a player focused on the Broken Pedestal quest, Observation is the branch needed for the dodge objective. For someone preparing Armament V2, base Armament progression is the relevant prerequisite. Choose your next branch around the task you want to finish, then return to other Haki paths afterwards.Conqueror Haki referenceOpen the separate branch card.Where Haki Is Required in Current QuestsThe Star Platinum Stardust route requires 50 successful Observation Haki dodges after the Broken Pedestal and earlier objectives.Keep Stardust 4 active when completing that counter. Test whether Observation’s successful dodges register before committing to a long fight. The objective is not a request to dash 50 times, and ordinary movement away from the enemy is not the same mechanic.Armament has its own progression gates for the later V2 route. Read the named stage and skill objective when training it. Quest conditions refer to a specific system, so a powerful style, a good race, or a defensive trait does not automatically replace Haki.Use the quest tracker to decide whether you need a new unlock or better execution of one you already own. If you have Observation but the dodge task stalls, test the action and stage. If you have basic Armament but cannot open V2, inspect the progression prerequisite rather than starting the base quests again.Which Haki Should You Unlock First?Choose Armament for its base strike progression, Observation when a dodge objective is your next blocker, and Armament V2 after its base prerequisites are ready.For a new Haki routine, begin with a short unlock checklist: required NPC, accepted task, target or skill, and money. Finish the current counter and read the next prompt. This is easier to follow than mixing several island farms into one session without checking which quests are active.For an established build, let the next unlock guide your order. Someone entering the Star Platinum dodge stage should prepare Observation. Someone with Stage 8 Armament can plan Ryou. If neither prerequisite is ready, spend the session finishing the earlier stage instead of travelling between advanced NPCs.Common Haki Unlock ProblemsMost stalled Haki tasks need a check of the named branch, quest stage, target type, or equipped Combat action.For Armament, confirm Combat is used where required. For Observation, distinguish the Hollow and Shinigami stages. For Ryou, check Stage 8 and the required Combat skill. For Stardust, confirm successful Observation dodges while the matching quest is active.Before repeating an activity, write down the counter and complete a small test. If progress changes, continue. If it stays unchanged, reread the objective and NPC dialogue. Diagnose the condition first; spending more money or fighting a harder enemy cannot solve an incorrectly selected quest.After an unlock, check the device’s actual controls and practise activation in a familiar fight. If the effect is absent, inspect whether it is available and active before judging the build. Keep Haki training separate from race or trait rerolls so the source of a problem remains clear.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhere do I start Armament Haki?Visit Rayleigh at Ice Land and follow the Combat-based unlock quests.Where do I unlock Observation Haki?Follow Enel’s route at Hollow Land, with the Hollow and Shinigami objectives.What is Ryou in Legacy Piece?Ryou is the name commonly used for the Armament Haki V2 / Busoshoku V2 progression.What do I need for Armament V2?Maxed Armament at Stage 8, 10,000,000 Money, and completion of Awaken Ryou 1 and 2.Does dashing count for the Star Platinum Haki quest?The task asks for successful Observation Haki dodges, not ordinary movement or repeated dash inputs.Is Conqueror the same as Armament V2?No. Conqueror is a separate Haki branch; Armament V2 is the later Armament progression.Why do Combat skill uses not count?Check the active quest, its prerequisite stage, and that you are using the named Combat skill.Related GuidesBroken PedestalFind the Broken Pedestal on Grave Island in Legacy Piece, start the Stardust route with Jotaro, and prepare Star Platinum’s Observation Haki task.Wild HuntUnlock Wild Hunt in Legacy Piece: four Memories, 1,000 Souls, Graveyard Island, Coffin Escort, Pearl methods, and the later crafting route.RacesLearn how Legacy Piece races shape damage and survival, compare current race roles, and decide which rolls to keep for melee, weapon, or flexible builds.TraitsLegacy Piece trait tier list comparing combat roles, current rarity groups, and when to keep a useful roll or spend trait rerolls.Tier ListA September 2026 Legacy Piece tier list covering the strongest ability and style targets, plus quick race, clan, trait, and fruit choices by playstyle.WikiLegacy Piece Wiki for Gwynn’s Shrine’s Roblox game: browse codes, quests, races, clans, traits, Haki, Wild Hunt, and community resources.

If your target is The World Over Heaven, first finish and enhance The World; the later Over Heaven route is a separate upgrade path. This distinction saves a lot of wasted searching because pages often use “Dio” for the NPC, the world boss, the base style, and the Over Heaven content interchangeably.Start from the current Roblox experience by Gwynn's Shrine, place ID 111097829542198. Legacy Piece search results also include material for a different, older Roblox title. In this guide, Dio means the current game's Ruin City and Joestar route.Legacy Piece resource linksOpen the current game page and community references.Where to Find Dio in Legacy PieceTravel to Ruin City and look for the Dio quest NPC. That is the starting point for the base style chain, rather than a random fruit spawn or a menu-only unlock.Speak to the NPC with the Joestar clan equipped. The starting dialogue is the first useful check: if the route does not open, confirm the clan before farming more boss materials. The location is important because Ruin City also hosts other progression content, including world-boss summons, and players can easily confuse a summon table with the Dio quest contact. Follow the objective shown by the NPC after accepting the route, then return to him as each stage completes.For orientation, use the official Roblox game page to enter the current experience, then confirm your in-game area name is Ruin City. The first budget gets you into the questline; the second completes the arrow. A current route guide lists 30 Broken Stand Arrow Fragments, 15 Vampire Blood, $25,000,000, and Rank SS or higher for the Blood-Stained Stand Arrow. Fragments are tied to Dio kills in the chain. Collecting fragments before understanding the quest order may leave you doing extra runs, so read the live objective and save the materials as you go.The four quest stages include activating the Joestar Defy Fate effect, scoring boss kills while that effect is active, clearing a high-level boss challenge without dying, and collecting the fragments. The timing on the active-effect stage matters: a kill outside its window does not serve the same objective. For the deathless stage, a safe and repeatable fight is better than the fastest boss you can barely beat. Set up a target you can survive, activate the effect, and finish eligible bosses during that window. If a counter fails to move, review the active state and target level before repeating the fight. For the deathless stage, favor a route with predictable attacks and room to reposition. The goal is not to prove a peak-damage combo; it is to complete all required kills without resetting.Once fragments and Vampire Blood are ready, return to the crafting step. Carry enough Money and confirm the Rank gate in the interface. The Shadow Dio fight is the final base-style gate. Enter it only after you have practiced your movement and can finish a full damage rotation while preserving a defensive option. If you play in a group, agree on who holds the boss's attention so the fight remains readable.Legacy Piece codesClaim current resources before a long farm.Joestar in the clans guideUnderstand why this clan gates the Dio route.Defy Fate guideLearn how Joestar Resolve and Defy Fate work during the Dio quest.The World Versus The World Over HeavenThe World is the base Dio style. The World Over Heaven is the later, higher-end style associated with enhanced Dio progression; it should not be treated as the automatic reward for the first questline.After unlocking The World, the Over Heaven route calls for the base style at enhancement +10 and additional Ruin City proof quests. That creates a clear order: finish the base chain, invest in its enhancement, and only then begin the upgrade-specific objectives. An update that added DIO OH also introduced tournament content and the Eclipse Championship NPC, so the later route may intersect with systems a new player has not yet opened.In current editorial rankings, The World Over Heaven is valued for Time Stop, damage, and a supporting buff. Those strengths make it useful both as a main style and as part of a broader setup. The base The World remains meaningful while you progress because its time-control identity can support a build before the endgame upgrade is ready. Another is killing a special boss outside the Defy Fate window, which wastes a fight for the active-effect objective. A third is attempting the deathless challenge on the hardest available target rather than one you can clear steadily. Finally, players sometimes spend an arrow material or their saved Money elsewhere and arrive at the craft short of a requirement.During Shadow Dio, keep enough distance to read his attack start, avoid spending every movement tool at once, and commit your main damage after a safe opening. Time-based styles punish players who attack into a control window without an exit. Choose by the whole package, not rarity alone or one large percentage on a screenshot.AdvertisementCurrent clan role summaryClanKnown roleGood reason to keepBerserkerDamage and durability with a ramping passiveGeneral boss or mixed-content build.OkkotsuCooldown and defensive supportFrequent skill rotations and longer fights.KetsumeiHigh damage with a health tradeoffPlanned burst and careful survival.KagekiriCritical-hit pressureBuilds that can exploit crit windows.ShunraiMovement and fast engagementPvP chase or mobile rotations.HyouketsuChill and freeze controlCrowd control and safer group clearing.TekketsuDefensive staying powerSurviving a difficult boss or dungeon.JoestarDio route requirementOpening The World quest chain.Berserker is a versatile offensive and defensive pick, especially when fights last long enough for its pressure to build. Okkotsu is attractive to skill-heavy characters because cooldown reduction and damage reduction improve both rotation frequency and survival. Ketsumei is a high-output option that asks you to manage its cost. Kagekiri leans toward critical pressure, Shunrai toward movement, and Hyouketsu toward control. Tekketsu is a useful defensive alternative even though it sits below the rarest labels.Joestar has a separate kind of value: the base The World quest with Dio calls for it. If you are working on that path, the clan's route access can outweigh an abstract damage ranking. The table is a player-facing comparison of roles; current in-game descriptions remain the final check for the exact effect on your character.Overall Legacy Piece tier listCompare a clan pick with the rest of the build.What Clans Change in Legacy PieceClans add passive stats and effects alongside race and trait. They do not turn into a weapon or fruit; they change how well your chosen combat route performs.A clan with a broad damage bonus can be useful on many abilities, while cooldown reduction becomes more valuable when your strongest moves are gated by a long wait. Damage reduction can increase effective output because surviving one more attack lets you complete another full rotation. Movement or control can be the deciding factor in PvP even when a different clan shows a larger damage number.Clans also participate in unlock routes. Joestar is the clearest example here because the base Dio quest checks for that clan. If you have a planned style route, investigate any gate before replacing your current clan. The three persistent systems serve different functions: races supply a stat orientation, traits supply a distinctive effect, and clans can bridge the two with additional passives or a skill. A balanced combination often beats three choices that all overinvest in the same stat.Current Clan Names and EffectsCurrent-game references list ten clan names: Berserker, Hyouketsu, Joestar, Kagekiri, Ketsumei, Kusakabe, Okkotsu, Shinmon, Shunrai, and Tekketsu.Current clan names by practical roleRoleNamesWhat to inspectBroad damage and survivalBerserker, Okkotsu, TekketsuHow long the character stays in each fight.Aggressive burstKetsumei, KagekiriWhether the rotation can exploit the damage window.Mobility and controlShunrai, HyouketsuPvP positioning and enemy resistance.Route or build-specificJoestar, Kusakabe, ShinmonStyle requirements and current in-game skill text.The most useful way to scan this roster is by decision role. Berserker supplies a broad offense-and-survival package. Okkotsu supplies cooldown support and protection. Ketsumei is the riskier damage route. Kagekiri emphasizes critical hits, Shunrai mobility, Hyouketsu freezing control, and Tekketsu defense. Joestar carries an important unlock relationship with Dio. Kusakabe and Shinmon are also part of the current roster; read their live in-game panels when comparing them to a roll you already use.A fixed ranking of every clan hides the context that makes one good. A control-focused Hyouketsu may carry a dungeon group that already has enough damage. A Ketsumei user who repeatedly falls before finishing a boss phase gains little from its offensive ceiling. A Joestar user finishing the Dio chain may have an excellent reason to hold that clan until the style unlock is complete. Ketsumei belongs near that group for a player who can manage its health cost and convert the burst into faster wins, but it is less forgiving. Joestar becomes an S-tier route pick specifically while unlocking Dio's The World. These are different reasons to keep a roll, and one reason should not be silently substituted for another.A tier covers focused winners such as Kagekiri for crit pressure, Shunrai for movement, and Hyouketsu for control. Tekketsu sits in a strong situational tier because defense can carry underpowered accounts through content they otherwise fail. B tier is a useful clan that does not clearly match the current damage plan; C tier describes an actual mismatch, not a permanently bad name. The right tier shifts when you change your weapon, ability, or the mode you play most.Dio guideSee exactly why Joestar matters.Araya ability guidePlan a damage route that can use a matching clan.Best Clan for PvE, PvP, and a Damage BuildFor repeated PvE clears, broad damage and enough survival to finish the run are the priority. For PvP, mobility and control can be as important as a larger opening hit.Berserker is a safe broad choice when you want one clan to help across farming and bosses. Okkotsu stands out when the build depends on cycling skills; lower downtime means more chances to use your strongest attacks, and its defensive profile helps long encounters. Ketsumei is attractive for burst-focused players who already manage incoming damage well. In PvP, Shunrai's mobility or Hyouketsu's control may win exchanges that a stationary damage setup cannot even start.Do not judge a clan without the other permanent layers. A tanky race can free the clan slot for more damage. A survival trait may make a risky clan easier to use. A weapon-oriented race needs a clan that does not leave its sword rotation exposed to every counterattack. If the answer is “this clan is not the highest rarity,” wait and test it in the content you actually play. If the answer is “its buff targets a damage source I never use” or “I need Joestar to open Dio,” the decision is clearer. Note any title, quest, or style gate before replacing a route-specific roll.Code rewards change with each update. Check the current reward table and the live clan interface, then decide when you will stop rather than rolling until every reward is gone. A useful intermediate clan can carry an account while you farm a major ability or weapon. The best keep still depends on your build.AdvertisementLegacy Piece Trait Tier List: Quick RankingThis is an editorial ranking for the current Gwynn's Shrine game. S and A picks have described effects; B and C are decision bands for rolls whose value depends heavily on your setup.AdvertisementEditorial trait tiers by practical roleTierTrait or groupWhy it is consideredSWorld Breaker; Dominion; Astral CoreStrong repeated damage, control, or defensive value.APhoenix Rebirth; Black Hole; Tyrant KingPowerful survival or control with a more specific use case.BMythical and Legend rolls that match the buildKeep when the live effect supports the main rotation.CTemporary Common and Uncommon rollsUseful while progressing; compare before heavy reroll spending.World Breaker has a clear boss-damage use because repeated hits on one target build pressure. Dominion contributes control and team value in an area. Astral Core combines a defensive shield with a follow-up attack. Those three are broadly useful in different fights, so the order between them changes with the content. Phoenix Rebirth can be a lifesaver in difficult solo clears, Black Hole helps hold enemies together, and Tyrant King favors a durable close-range setup.A rarity label alone is not a fight result. If your current trait keeps a boss run stable, replacing it with a rare name that does not activate in your rotation can be a downgrade. Use the tier below as a shortlist, then compare how often the effect triggers during your actual play.Overall Legacy Piece tier listSee where traits fit with races and clans.What Traits Change in Legacy PieceTraits are a persistent character layer alongside race and clan. A trait may alter damage, protection, control, or recovery without changing your equipped weapon or style.That makes traits easy to undervalue. A strong passive may add an attack after a fixed number of hits, keep you alive through a bad boss phase, or create room for a group to finish a target. The key is trigger frequency. A passive that activates once in a long duel may be excellent for PvP but unimpressive during quick ordinary mob kills. Another that stacks on every hit can be outstanding on a stationary boss yet weak when you constantly switch targets.The current game has a substantial trait pool, and its upper rarities are extremely hard to target through random rerolls. A practical account plan starts with a good-enough effect that supports your current weapon or ability, then saves surplus rerolls for a more deliberate chase. Check current reward details before planning around any reroll source, and do not discard a trait that already solves your hardest content just to pursue a rare label.Current Legacy Piece Traits by RarityThe current Trello-derived roster groups 26 named traits across Secret, Mythical, Legend, Epic, Rare, Uncommon, and Common rarities. The table is a name reference; the tier above ranks combat roles, not every name in a vacuum.Trait names in the current rosterRarityNamesPlanning noteSecretAstral Core, Black Hole, Dominion, Phoenix Rebirth, Tyrant King, World BreakerCompare the signature passive to your main content.MythicalAscension, Flashstep, Limitless, Malevolent, Supreme WillRead the live effect before rerolling a matching one.LegendRebirth, Unstoppable, WarlordEvaluate the exact in-game tooltip.EpicAwakened, Breaker, OverdriveOften useful as an intermediate keep.RarePredator, Sharpened, ViciousJudge synergy with your main damage type.UncommonDriven, Equilibrium, SteadyProgression rolls while building resources.CommonBrutal, Iron Skin, SwiftEarly effects to replace selectively.Secret traits have the most described signature effects. A name that sounds aggressive does not necessarily help a defensive build, and a common utility effect can still be useful while you are leveling.How the Leading Secret Traits PlayThe six named Secret traits do not all solve the same problem. Focus on the effect that fills a gap in your build.World Breaker rewards staying on one target across successive hits, making it an obvious boss-farming candidate. Dominion sets up a controlled area and adds team pressure; players who fight in groups or need to hold enemies in place may value it more than a pure personal-damage roll. Astral Core adds a shield and follow-up attack, helping a player survive while keeping pressure on a target.Black Hole is useful for pulling enemies together and disrupting their movement. Phoenix Rebirth turns a lethal moment into another chance, which can protect an expensive attempt or an unfamiliar dungeon run. Tyrant King favors a durable, close-range character that can remain in danger long enough to benefit from its defensive and sustain effects. None of those descriptions means one Secret is automatically best in all modes. Their value changes when a boss is immune to control, when an arena scatters targets, or when a group already provides enough survival.Araya ability guideSee a damage route that can benefit from repeated pressure.Dio style guideCompare a control-focused style route.Best Trait Direction for PvE, PvP, and GrindingFor a single boss, ask whether the trait improves the full damage cycle or protects the run from failure. For PvP, ask whether it creates a safe opening or preserves momentum after a trade.World Breaker is easiest to justify when hits stay on one target. Astral Core and Phoenix Rebirth can matter more in solo PvE where a death resets progress. Dominion and Black Hole have obvious control value in crowded encounters, though a target's resistance and movement still matter. During fast ordinary grinding, effects that need a long buildup may activate too late to influence most packs, while area control and reliable defense can make the route smoother.Compare your trait with the race and clan already equipped. A build with abundant damage but weak survival may gain more from Astral Core than another offensive layer. A tanky race and Berserker clan may free the trait slot for pressure. A cooldown-focused Okkotsu setup can capitalize on a trait that rewards frequent skill use. This is why the site separates traits, races, and clans into detailed pages, even though they all contribute to one build.Race guideMatch a passive stat line to the trait.Clan guideCompare damage and survival layers.When to Keep or Reroll a TraitKeep a trait if it improves a repeatable fight you actually do and you lack enough rerolls to replace it comfortably. Reroll when the effect conflicts with your main damage route or your account can absorb the gamble.Before pressing reroll, write down the trait's job: single-target damage, crowd control, survival, mobility, or a specific support effect. Then choose the job you need next. If the current trait already fills that job, rarity chasing becomes a poor reason to spend. If it activates rarely in your normal content, a different effect may be worth pursuing even if the new rarity is not the absolute highest.When you acquire Trait Rerolls, check the live trait menu and decide a stopping point before rolling. Code rewards change with each update, so read the current reward list instead of budgeting an assumed amount. Read the current Conqueror card and the game’s unlock prompt before committing resources to that path.For a player focused on the Broken Pedestal quest, Observation is the branch needed for the dodge objective. For someone preparing Armament V2, base Armament progression is the relevant prerequisite. Choose your next branch around the task you want to finish, then return to other Haki paths afterwards.Conqueror Haki referenceOpen the separate branch card.Where Haki Is Required in Current QuestsThe Star Platinum Stardust route requires 50 successful Observation Haki dodges after the Broken Pedestal and earlier objectives.Keep Stardust 4 active when completing that counter. Test whether Observation’s successful dodges register before committing to a long fight. The objective is not a request to dash 50 times, and ordinary movement away from the enemy is not the same mechanic.Armament has its own progression gates for the later V2 route. Read the named stage and skill objective when training it. Quest conditions refer to a specific system, so a powerful style, a good race, or a defensive trait does not automatically replace Haki.Use the quest tracker to decide whether you need a new unlock or better execution of one you already own. If you have Observation but the dodge task stalls, test the action and stage. If you have basic Armament but cannot open V2, inspect the progression prerequisite rather than starting the base quests again.Which Haki Should You Unlock First?Choose Armament for its base strike progression, Observation when a dodge objective is your next blocker, and Armament V2 after its base prerequisites are ready.For a new Haki routine, begin with a short unlock checklist: required NPC, accepted task, target or skill, and money. Finish the current counter and read the next prompt. This is easier to follow than mixing several island farms into one session without checking which quests are active.For an established build, let the next unlock guide your order. Someone entering the Star Platinum dodge stage should prepare Observation. Someone with Stage 8 Armament can plan Ryou. If neither prerequisite is ready, spend the session finishing the earlier stage instead of travelling between advanced NPCs.Common Haki Unlock ProblemsMost stalled Haki tasks need a check of the named branch, quest stage, target type, or equipped Combat action.For Armament, confirm Combat is used where required. For Observation, distinguish the Hollow and Shinigami stages. For Ryou, check Stage 8 and the required Combat skill. For Stardust, confirm successful Observation dodges while the matching quest is active.Before repeating an activity, write down the counter and complete a small test. If progress changes, continue. If it stays unchanged, reread the objective and NPC dialogue. Diagnose the condition first; spending more money or fighting a harder enemy cannot solve an incorrectly selected quest.After an unlock, check the device’s actual controls and practise activation in a familiar fight. If the effect is absent, inspect whether it is available and active before judging the build. Keep Haki training separate from race or trait rerolls so the source of a problem remains clear.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhere do I start Armament Haki?Visit Rayleigh at Ice Land and follow the Combat-based unlock quests.Where do I unlock Observation Haki?Follow Enel’s route at Hollow Land, with the Hollow and Shinigami objectives.What is Ryou in Legacy Piece?Ryou is the name commonly used for the Armament Haki V2 / Busoshoku V2 progression.What do I need for Armament V2?Maxed Armament at Stage 8, 10,000,000 Money, and completion of Awaken Ryou 1 and 2.Does dashing count for the Star Platinum Haki quest?The task asks for successful Observation Haki dodges, not ordinary movement or repeated dash inputs.Is Conqueror the same as Armament V2?No. Conqueror is a separate Haki branch; Armament V2 is the later Armament progression.Why do Combat skill uses not count?Check the active quest, its prerequisite stage, and that you are using the named Combat skill.Related GuidesBroken PedestalFind the Broken Pedestal on Grave Island in Legacy Piece, start the Stardust route with Jotaro, and prepare Star Platinum’s Observation Haki task.Wild HuntUnlock Wild Hunt in Legacy Piece: four Memories, 1,000 Souls, Graveyard Island, Coffin Escort, Pearl methods, and the later crafting route.RacesLearn how Legacy Piece races shape damage and survival, compare current race roles, and decide which rolls to keep for melee, weapon, or flexible builds.TraitsLegacy Piece trait tier list comparing combat roles, current rarity groups, and when to keep a useful roll or spend trait rerolls.Tier ListA September 2026 Legacy Piece tier list covering the strongest ability and style targets, plus quick race, clan, trait, and fruit choices by playstyle.WikiLegacy Piece Wiki for Gwynn’s Shrine’s Roblox game: browse codes, quests, races, clans, traits, Haki, Wild Hunt, and community resources.

The route starts with the Joestar clan and a Money payment, continues through a four-part challenge, and ends with a Shadow Dio fight in The Stopped World.AdvertisementDio route at a glanceGoalWhere it beginsWhat to prepareBase The WorldDio NPC in Ruin CityJoestar clan, Money, quest progress, arrow materialsShadow Dio encounterThe Stopped World after the arrow craftA reliable boss build and full quest completionThe World Over HeavenLater Dio upgrade routeBase The World enhanced to +10, then new Ruin City objectivesThe short planning sequence is: equip Joestar, talk to Dio in Ruin City, complete his quests in order, craft the Blood-Stained Stand Arrow, and beat Shadow Dio. If your target is The World Over Heaven, first finish and enhance The World; the later Over Heaven route is a separate upgrade path. This distinction saves a lot of wasted searching because pages often use “Dio” for the NPC, the world boss, the base style, and the Over Heaven content interchangeably.Start from the current Roblox experience by Gwynn's Shrine, place ID 111097829542198. Legacy Piece search results also include material for a different, older Roblox title. In this guide, Dio means the current game's Ruin City and Joestar route.Legacy Piece resource linksOpen the current game page and community references.Where to Find Dio in Legacy PieceTravel to Ruin City and look for the Dio quest NPC. That is the starting point for the base style chain, rather than a random fruit spawn or a menu-only unlock.Speak to the NPC with the Joestar clan equipped. The starting dialogue is the first useful check: if the route does not open, confirm the clan before farming more boss materials. The location is important because Ruin City also hosts other progression content, including world-boss summons, and players can easily confuse a summon table with the Dio quest contact. Follow the objective shown by the NPC after accepting the route, then return to him as each stage completes.For orientation, use the official Roblox game page to enter the current experience, then confirm your in-game area name is Ruin City. Avoid relying on an old island map that names a different experience with the same title. When an update rearranges NPC positions, the area and quest dialogue are better anchors than a screenshot of one exact coordinate.Dio Requirements and the Base The World UnlockThe base quest starts with the Joestar clan and a $5,000,000 payment to Dio. The later arrow craft has its own rank, material, and Money requirements.Base The World route requirementsCheckpointRequirementPractical noteOpen the Dio chainJoestar clan; $5,000,000Check the NPC dialogue before farming.Quest chainFour sequential objectivesRead the live counter after each stage.Craft the arrow30 Broken Stand Arrow Fragments; 15 Vampire Blood; $25,000,000; Rank SS+Keep these materials reserved for the craft.Final encounterDefeat Shadow Dio in The Stopped WorldEnter with a tested boss rotation.Treat the route as two budgets. The first budget gets you into the questline; the second completes the arrow. A current route guide lists 30 Broken Stand Arrow Fragments, 15 Vampire Blood, $25,000,000, and Rank SS or higher for the Blood-Stained Stand Arrow. Fragments are tied to Dio kills in the chain. Collecting fragments before understanding the quest order may leave you doing extra runs, so read the live objective and save the materials as you go.The four quest stages include activating the Joestar Defy Fate effect, scoring boss kills while that effect is active, clearing a high-level boss challenge without dying, and collecting the fragments. The timing on the active-effect stage matters: a kill outside its window does not serve the same objective. For the deathless stage, a safe and repeatable fight is better than the fastest boss you can barely beat. Set up a target you can survive, activate the effect, and finish eligible bosses during that window. If a counter fails to move, review the active state and target level before repeating the fight. For the deathless stage, favor a route with predictable attacks and room to reposition. The goal is not to prove a peak-damage combo; it is to complete all required kills without resetting.Once fragments and Vampire Blood are ready, return to the crafting step. Carry enough Money and confirm the Rank gate in the interface. The Shadow Dio fight is the final base-style gate. Enter it only after you have practiced your movement and can finish a full damage rotation while preserving a defensive option. If you play in a group, agree on who holds the boss's attention so the fight remains readable.Legacy Piece codesClaim current resources before a long farm.Joestar in the clans guideUnderstand why this clan gates the Dio route.Defy Fate guideLearn how Joestar Resolve and Defy Fate work during the Dio quest.The World Versus The World Over HeavenThe World is the base Dio style. The World Over Heaven is the later, higher-end style associated with enhanced Dio progression; it should not be treated as the automatic reward for the first questline.After unlocking The World, the Over Heaven route calls for the base style at enhancement +10 and additional Ruin City proof quests. That creates a clear order: finish the base chain, invest in its enhancement, and only then begin the upgrade-specific objectives. An update that added DIO OH also introduced tournament content and the Eclipse Championship NPC, so the later route may intersect with systems a new player has not yet opened.In current editorial rankings, The World Over Heaven is valued for Time Stop, damage, and a supporting buff. Those strengths make it useful both as a main style and as part of a broader setup. The base The World remains meaningful while you progress because its time-control identity can support a build before the endgame upgrade is ready. If your account is still short on rank or materials, enjoy the base style and make the upgrade a planned project instead of an immediate assumption.Legacy Piece tier listCompare Dio’s style with other current targets.Araya guideCompare a high-damage ability path with the Dio style path.The World Over Heaven guideFollow the dedicated DIO OH upgrade route and requirements.Shadow Dio Fight Tips and Common MistakesA clean boss attempt begins before the arena: bring your best reliable rotation, check survival tools, and know which quest counter you are advancing.The most common route error is entering without Joestar, then assuming the Dio NPC is broken. Another is killing a special boss outside the Defy Fate window, which wastes a fight for the active-effect objective. A third is attempting the deathless challenge on the hardest available target rather than one you can clear steadily. Finally, players sometimes spend an arrow material or their saved Money elsewhere and arrive at the craft short of a requirement.During Shadow Dio, keep enough distance to read his attack start, avoid spending every movement tool at once, and commit your main damage after a safe opening. Time-based styles punish players who attack into a control window without an exit. If you fail, identify whether the loss came from low damage, an avoidable hit, or a missing build layer, then change one thing for the next attempt. Berserker brings broad damage and durability, Okkotsu supports uptime, and Joestar matters for the Dio route.AdvertisementLegacy Piece Clans: Quick ComparisonA clan can supply base stats, a passive effect, and a skill. Choose by the whole package, not rarity alone or one large percentage on a screenshot.AdvertisementCurrent clan role summaryClanKnown roleGood reason to keepBerserkerDamage and durability with a ramping passiveGeneral boss or mixed-content build.OkkotsuCooldown and defensive supportFrequent skill rotations and longer fights.KetsumeiHigh damage with a health tradeoffPlanned burst and careful survival.KagekiriCritical-hit pressureBuilds that can exploit crit windows.ShunraiMovement and fast engagementPvP chase or mobile rotations.HyouketsuChill and freeze controlCrowd control and safer group clearing.TekketsuDefensive staying powerSurviving a difficult boss or dungeon.JoestarDio route requirementOpening The World quest chain.Berserker is a versatile offensive and defensive pick, especially when fights last long enough for its pressure to build. Okkotsu is attractive to skill-heavy characters because cooldown reduction and damage reduction improve both rotation frequency and survival. Ketsumei is a high-output option that asks you to manage its cost. Kagekiri leans toward critical pressure, Shunrai toward movement, and Hyouketsu toward control. Tekketsu is a useful defensive alternative even though it sits below the rarest labels.Joestar has a separate kind of value: the base The World quest with Dio calls for it. If you are working on that path, the clan's route access can outweigh an abstract damage ranking. The table is a player-facing comparison of roles; current in-game descriptions remain the final check for the exact effect on your character.Overall Legacy Piece tier listCompare a clan pick with the rest of the build.What Clans Change in Legacy PieceClans add passive stats and effects alongside race and trait. They do not turn into a weapon or fruit; they change how well your chosen combat route performs.A clan with a broad damage bonus can be useful on many abilities, while cooldown reduction becomes more valuable when your strongest moves are gated by a long wait. Damage reduction can increase effective output because surviving one more attack lets you complete another full rotation. Movement or control can be the deciding factor in PvP even when a different clan shows a larger damage number.Clans also participate in unlock routes. Joestar is the clearest example here because the base Dio quest checks for that clan. If you have a planned style route, investigate any gate before replacing your current clan. The three persistent systems serve different functions: races supply a stat orientation, traits supply a distinctive effect, and clans can bridge the two with additional passives or a skill. A balanced combination often beats three choices that all overinvest in the same stat.Current Clan Names and EffectsCurrent-game references list ten clan names: Berserker, Hyouketsu, Joestar, Kagekiri, Ketsumei, Kusakabe, Okkotsu, Shinmon, Shunrai, and Tekketsu.Current clan names by practical roleRoleNamesWhat to inspectBroad damage and survivalBerserker, Okkotsu, TekketsuHow long the character stays in each fight.Aggressive burstKetsumei, KagekiriWhether the rotation can exploit the damage window.Mobility and controlShunrai, HyouketsuPvP positioning and enemy resistance.Route or build-specificJoestar, Kusakabe, ShinmonStyle requirements and current in-game skill text.The most useful way to scan this roster is by decision role. Berserker supplies a broad offense-and-survival package. Okkotsu supplies cooldown support and protection. Ketsumei is the riskier damage route. Kagekiri emphasizes critical hits, Shunrai mobility, Hyouketsu freezing control, and Tekketsu defense. Joestar carries an important unlock relationship with Dio. Kusakabe and Shinmon are also part of the current roster; read their live in-game panels when comparing them to a roll you already use.A fixed ranking of every clan hides the context that makes one good. A control-focused Hyouketsu may carry a dungeon group that already has enough damage. A Ketsumei user who repeatedly falls before finishing a boss phase gains little from its offensive ceiling. A Joestar user finishing the Dio chain may have an excellent reason to hold that clan until the style unlock is complete. Record why you keep a clan so future rerolls have a clear target.Legacy Piece Clan Tier List by Build GoalThe following tiers are editorial and reward usable power in a real build. They are not a statement that the developer ranks one clan officially above another.Editorial clan tiersTierExamplesWho benefitsSBerserker; Okkotsu; Ketsumei with a suitable buildBroad power or high-output rotation.S for routeJoestar while pursuing DioPlayers working on The World unlock.AKagekiri; Shunrai; HyouketsuCrit, mobility, or control specialists.BTekketsu and other good situational keepsSurvival-first progression.CAny clan whose effects rarely trigger in your buildConsider rerolling only with a clear target.S tier includes Berserker for wide applicability and Okkotsu for a dependable mix of uptime and defense. Ketsumei belongs near that group for a player who can manage its health cost and convert the burst into faster wins, but it is less forgiving. Joestar becomes an S-tier route pick specifically while unlocking Dio's The World. These are different reasons to keep a roll, and one reason should not be silently substituted for another.A tier covers focused winners such as Kagekiri for crit pressure, Shunrai for movement, and Hyouketsu for control. Tekketsu sits in a strong situational tier because defense can carry underpowered accounts through content they otherwise fail. B tier is a useful clan that does not clearly match the current damage plan; C tier describes an actual mismatch, not a permanently bad name. The right tier shifts when you change your weapon, ability, or the mode you play most.Dio guideSee exactly why Joestar matters.Araya ability guidePlan a damage route that can use a matching clan.Best Clan for PvE, PvP, and a Damage BuildFor repeated PvE clears, broad damage and enough survival to finish the run are the priority. For PvP, mobility and control can be as important as a larger opening hit.Berserker is a safe broad choice when you want one clan to help across farming and bosses. Okkotsu stands out when the build depends on cycling skills; lower downtime means more chances to use your strongest attacks, and its defensive profile helps long encounters. Ketsumei is attractive for burst-focused players who already manage incoming damage well. In PvP, Shunrai's mobility or Hyouketsu's control may win exchanges that a stationary damage setup cannot even start.Do not judge a clan without the other permanent layers. A tanky race can free the clan slot for more damage. A survival trait may make a risky clan easier to use. A weapon-oriented race needs a clan that does not leave its sword rotation exposed to every counterattack. The tier list gives a direction, then the races and traits pages help finish the combination.Legacy Piece racesMatch clan effects to a race passive.Legacy Piece traitsComplete the damage and survival layers.Legacy Piece fruitsSee how a fruit ability fits the same build.When to Keep or Reroll a ClanKeep a clan when its effects help your main rotation or unlock path. Reroll when you have a defined upgrade target, enough currency to handle bad luck, and no current quest that depends on the clan.A sensible reroll plan begins with the reason you want to leave the current clan. If the answer is “this clan is not the highest rarity,” wait and test it in the content you actually play. If the answer is “its buff targets a damage source I never use” or “I need Joestar to open Dio,” the decision is clearer. Note any title, quest, or style gate before replacing a route-specific roll.Code rewards change with each update. Check the current reward table and the live clan interface, then decide when you will stop rather than rolling until every reward is gone. A useful intermediate clan can carry an account while you farm a major ability or weapon. After that unlock, review the clan again against the new rotation; rerolling becomes more valuable when you know what the finished build needs.Legacy Piece codesCollect reroll resources.Legacy Piece resourcesCheck current game and community notes.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhich Legacy Piece clans are best?Berserker is a broad damage-and-survival choice, while Okkotsu helps cooldown-focused builds. Reroll only when you have a more valuable target for your build.Does a Clan Reroll change my race or trait?Clans, races, and traits are separate build systems. Check the active objective before changing races so you do not remove the prerequisite for your planned unlock."}}]}]Home › Undead FishmanLegacy Piece GuideLegacy Piece Undead FishmanFollow the quest-linked Legacy Piece Fishman progression toward Undead Fishman, check your current race stage, and avoid wasting rerolls before the route is complete.AdvertisementLast reviewed: October 3, 2026How to Get Undead Fishman in Legacy PieceEquip Fishman and talk to the Fishman Elder on Fishman Island. Complete the Undead Fishman quest, gather the evolution materials, and return to the Elder for the race unlock.AdvertisementUndead Fishman is a quest-linked race, so treating it as an ordinary reroll target misses the main route. Start by checking the race actually equipped on your character. Then choose the matching evolution objective at the Elder before farming its items. Quest progress and the final material collection are separate checkpoints.The current race card supplies both the opening objective and the turn-in list. Use it alongside the material cards when deciding what to farm next. If you already have Fishman, preserve it while you work through this route. Changing races for a general tier recommendation before the unlock can remove the named prerequisite you still need.Undead Fishman race cardRead the Fishman Elder route and listed effects.Legacy Piece races guideCompare quest-linked races with ordinary race choices.Fishman to Ancient Fishman and Undead FishmanFishman, Ancient Fishman, and Undead Fishman belong to quest-linked progression. The Undead Fishman card names base Fishman as its prerequisite; it does not list Ancient Fishman as a required earlier stage.That distinction matters when planning a farm. Do not assume the three names form one mandatory sequence just because they appear together in a race roster. Read the evolution you want and select its own quest. The Ancient Fishman and Undead Fishman materials have similar names, but an Ancient Scale is not an Undead Scale.If you searched for the Ancient Fishman race in Legacy Piece while trying to unlock Undead Fishman, check which destination you intended. The names identify different race entries. A guide about one evolution should not become the material checklist for the other. Use the Elder's active objective and your inventory labels to keep them apart.Undead Fishman RequirementsThe opening quest asks for five Fishman Captain defeats and three Undead Fishman Scales. The final evolution uses 20 Undead Fishman Scales, five Undead Fishman Cores, 100 Dreadtide Fangs, and 50 Dreadtide Hearts.Undead Fishman unlock checklistStageRequired checkPurposeStarting raceFishman equippedOpen the Fishman Elder routeQuest objective5 Fishman Captains; 3 Undead Fishman ScalesComplete the initial questEvolution materials20 Undead Fishman Scales; 5 Undead Fishman CoresPrepare the final collectionDreadtide materials100 Dreadtide Fangs; 50 Dreadtide HeartsComplete the remaining turn-inFinishReturn to Fishman ElderExchange the required materials for the raceTalk to the Elder with Fishman equipped before building your farming plan. This makes the order important: first open the route, then complete the initial objective, then finish the later collection.Scales and Cores are linked to Fishman Captain, while the Dreadtide material cards identify Dreadtide Revenant as their source. Focus on the missing item rather than repeating whichever boss you fought most recently. Check the relevant material card and active stage when a farm is not producing the item you need.Undead Fishman Scale referenceCheck the quest condition and required totals.Undead Fishman Core referenceCheck when the Core farm becomes available.What Undead Fishman Does for a BuildThe race card lists lifesteal, damage bonus, HP regeneration, and damage reduction. Its Undying Depths passive adds Soul shards and a conditional survival effect.The listed base effects are 12% lifesteal, 15% damage bonus, 6 HP regeneration per second, and 15% damage reduction. Undying Depths has three Soul shards, each adding 8% lifesteal. With all three present, a lethal blow shatters them and restores 25% of maximum HP; a shattered shard returns every 45 seconds.Those effects make sustain and repeated fight completion useful reasons to consider the race. Test how often you can finish a rotation and recover between dangerous attacks. A survival effect is conditional, so do not plan every encounter as if it were always available. A reroll changes the race you are relying on for this unlock.Before spending a Race Reroll, check whether the next objective still names your equipped race. A general damage recommendation is less useful if changing to it interrupts the quest you are trying to finish. Complete the planned unlock first, then decide whether another race suits your long-term build.Do not rely on a code reward as a guaranteed way to recover the same race afterward. Reroll resources help you make another attempt; they do not replace an evolution quest or promise a particular result. Keep the codes guide separate from your route checklist so a resource claim does not become an assumption about unlock completion.Common Undead Fishman Unlock ProblemsCheck the equipped race, chosen evolution quest, five-Captain counter, and exact material names before repeating the farm.If the Elder does not offer the expected route, inspect the equipped race and current quest stage. If the counter is unfinished, focus on eligible Fishman Captain defeats and the quest's Undead Scales. The best keep still depends on your build.AdvertisementLegacy Piece Trait Tier List: Quick RankingThis is an editorial ranking for the current Gwynn's Shrine game. S and A picks have described effects; B and C are decision bands for rolls whose value depends heavily on your setup.AdvertisementEditorial trait tiers by practical roleTierTrait or groupWhy it is consideredSWorld Breaker; Dominion; Astral CoreStrong repeated damage, control, or defensive value.APhoenix Rebirth; Black Hole; Tyrant KingPowerful survival or control with a more specific use case.BMythical and Legend rolls that match the buildKeep when the live effect supports the main rotation.CTemporary Common and Uncommon rollsUseful while progressing; compare before heavy reroll spending.World Breaker has a clear boss-damage use because repeated hits on one target build pressure. Dominion contributes control and team value in an area. Astral Core combines a defensive shield with a follow-up attack. Those three are broadly useful in different fights, so the order between them changes with the content. Phoenix Rebirth can be a lifesaver in difficult solo clears, Black Hole helps hold enemies together, and Tyrant King favors a durable close-range setup.A rarity label alone is not a fight result. If your current trait keeps a boss run stable, replacing it with a rare name that does not activate in your rotation can be a downgrade. Use the tier below as a shortlist, then compare how often the effect triggers during your actual play.Overall Legacy Piece tier listSee where traits fit with races and clans.What Traits Change in Legacy PieceTraits are a persistent character layer alongside race and clan. A trait may alter damage, protection, control, or recovery without changing your equipped weapon or style.That makes traits easy to undervalue. A strong passive may add an attack after a fixed number of hits, keep you alive through a bad boss phase, or create room for a group to finish a target. The key is trigger frequency. A passive that activates once in a long duel may be excellent for PvP but unimpressive during quick ordinary mob kills. Another that stacks on every hit can be outstanding on a stationary boss yet weak when you constantly switch targets.The current game has a substantial trait pool, and its upper rarities are extremely hard to target through random rerolls. A practical account plan starts with a good-enough effect that supports your current weapon or ability, then saves surplus rerolls for a more deliberate chase. Dominion sets up a controlled area and adds team pressure; players who fight in groups or need to hold enemies in place may value it more than a pure personal-damage roll. Astral Core adds a shield and follow-up attack, helping a player survive while keeping pressure on a target.Black Hole is useful for pulling enemies together and disrupting their movement. Phoenix Rebirth turns a lethal moment into another chance, which can protect an expensive attempt or an unfamiliar dungeon run. Tyrant King favors a durable, close-range character that can remain in danger long enough to benefit from its defensive and sustain effects. None of those descriptions means one Secret is automatically best in all modes. Their value changes when a boss is immune to control, when an arena scatters targets, or when a group already provides enough survival.Araya ability guideSee a damage route that can benefit from repeated pressure.Dio style guideCompare a control-focused style route.Best Trait Direction for PvE, PvP, and GrindingFor a single boss, ask whether the trait improves the full damage cycle or protects the run from failure. Dominion and Black Hole have obvious control value in crowded encounters, though a target's resistance and movement still matter. If your target is The World Over Heaven, first finish and enhance The World; the later Over Heaven route is a separate upgrade path. In this guide, Dio means the current game's Ruin City and Joestar route.Legacy Piece resource linksOpen the current game page and community references.Where to Find Dio in Legacy PieceTravel to Ruin City and look for the Dio quest NPC. That is the starting point for the base style chain, rather than a random fruit spawn or a menu-only unlock.Speak to the NPC with the Joestar clan equipped. The starting dialogue is the first useful check: if the route does not open, confirm the clan before farming more boss materials. The location is important because Ruin City also hosts other progression content, including world-boss summons, and players can easily confuse a summon table with the Dio quest contact. Follow the objective shown by the NPC after accepting the route, then return to him as each stage completes.For orientation, use the official Roblox game page to enter the current experience, then confirm your in-game area name is Ruin City. Carry enough Money and confirm the Rank gate in the interface. The Shadow Dio fight is the final base-style gate. Enter it only after you have practiced your movement and can finish a full damage rotation while preserving a defensive option. If you play in a group, agree on who holds the boss's attention so the fight remains readable.Legacy Piece codesClaim current resources before a long farm.Joestar in the clans guideUnderstand why this clan gates the Dio route.Defy Fate guideLearn how Joestar Resolve and Defy Fate work during the Dio quest.The World Versus The World Over HeavenThe World is the base Dio style. The World Over Heaven is the later, higher-end style associated with enhanced Dio progression; it should not be treated as the automatic reward for the first questline.After unlocking The World, the Over Heaven route calls for the base style at enhancement +10 and additional Ruin City proof quests. That creates a clear order: finish the base chain, invest in its enhancement, and only then begin the upgrade-specific objectives. An update that added DIO OH also introduced tournament content and the Eclipse Championship NPC, so the later route may intersect with systems a new player has not yet opened.In current editorial rankings, The World Over Heaven is valued for Time Stop, damage, and a supporting buff. Those strengths make it useful both as a main style and as part of a broader setup. Those counters do not advance in the same way.Star Platinum Quest Requirements After the PedestalThe next Stardust objectives are 40 Special Boss defeats, 50 Starlight Shards, 50 Observation Haki dodges, and 25 Starlight Cores.Objectives following the pedestalStageRequirementWhat to watchStardust 240 Special Boss defeatsEligible boss classificationStardust 350 Starlight ShardsShard quest activeStardust 450 Observation Haki dodgesSuccessful Haki dodgesStardust 525 Starlight CoresCore quest activeSpecial Bosses are the eligible summoned or rotation encounters named by the route, rather than every fixed-spawn enemy. Start with a manageable eligible target and confirm one kill counts before committing to the full set. A faster ordinary enemy does not help if it falls outside the requested category.Starlight Shards and Starlight Cores are different items. Their drops are tied to their matching Stardust stages, so do not spend hours trying to pre-farm a quest-locked collection. Inspect the active task and item name before each session. Keep the materials for the final exchange after the counters are complete.Observation Haki and the Pedestal QuestThe Stardust dodge task requires successful Observation Haki dodges. Ordinary movement away from an attack is a different action.Unlock Observation before tackling that stage, then watch the counter during an encounter you can control. Test a small set of incoming attacks and check that the objective advances. Pressing a movement key repeatedly is not proof that Observation’s dodge has triggered.Use a target with attacks you can observe without overwhelming your health. Stop after a short test to compare the counter with your starting value. Once you know the task registers, repeat the same reliable conditions instead of changing enemies after every attempt.Legacy Piece Haki guideUnlock Observation and understand its quest use.Broken Pedestal Not Working? Check These StepsCheck Grave Island, Jotaro’s dialogue, Joestar, the opening payment, and whether Stardust 1 is active.If no useful interaction appears, inspect the quest tracker first. If it names a later Stardust task, you may already have completed the pedestal stage. Follow that task instead of repeatedly interacting with the same object.If the next stage does not activate after completion, speak to Jotaro again. His dialogue can restore the first unfinished Stardust stage. Read the returned objective before farming, and keep the shard and core stages separate when diagnosing a missing drop.For a location problem, use the tracker distance and the purple crystal landmark. For a boss or material problem, use the stage’s conditions. This keeps the pedestal search from becoming a distraction when your actual blocker has moved to a later objective.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhich island has the Broken Pedestal?Grave Island. It is on the far side, deeper into the island from Jotaro’s location near the spawn.How do I recognise the Broken Pedestal?Look for the broken structure and nearby purple crystal, then follow the active quest tracker.What do I need to start the pedestal quest?Start Jotaro’s Stardust route with Joestar and $5,000,000, then follow the first objective.Does the pedestal give Star Platinum immediately?No. It completes the opening search stage; boss, material, Haki, and exchange requirements follow.Why do my Observation dodges not count?Check that Stardust 4 is active and that Observation Haki is performing the successful dodges.What if the next Stardust quest is missing?Speak to Jotaro again and read the restored unfinished stage before continuing.Related GuidesHakiUnlock Legacy Piece Armament and Observation Haki, prepare Armament V2 / Ryou, and understand the combat uses and Star Platinum dodge requirement.TrelloLegacy Piece Trello guide with the current board link, Roblox game identity check, key resource categories, and quick links for codes, builds, and quests.Tier ListA September 2026 Legacy Piece tier list covering the strongest ability and style targets, plus quick race, clan, trait, and fruit choices by playstyle.WikiLegacy Piece Wiki for Gwynn’s Shrine’s Roblox game: browse codes, quests, races, clans, traits, Haki, Wild Hunt, and community resources.
